questions.question: A vendor states that its system 'understands the intent behind a customer's message.' Under the Russell and Norvig taxonomy, this is a claim about:
Which of the following is inside artificial intelligence but outside machine learning?
The immediate cause of the collapse of the commercial expert system industry was:

options.A: Withdrawal of all government funding worldwide
options.B: Proof that rule-based reasoning is incorrect
options.C: The knowledge acquisition bottleneck and maintenance cost
options.D: The publication of the transformer architecture

questions.question: The 2012 ImageNet result mattered chiefly because:

options.A: It was the first use of neural networks
options.B: It proved artificial general intelligence is achievable
options.C: The margin over the previous state of the art was too large to attribute to tuning

questions.question: The Turing test is no longer used as a research target primarily because:

options.A: Turing withdrew it in a later paper
options.B: No system has ever passed it
options.C: It rewards imitation of human limitations rather than useful capability
options.D: It is computationally intractable to administer

questions.question: The physical symbol system hypothesis was articulated by:
Which statement about deployed artificial intelligence in 2026 is accurate?

options.A: Several systems have achieved general intelligence
options.C: Narrow systems cannot be commercially useful
options.D: Narrow and general differ only in training data volume

questions.question: A team wants to build an examination timetabling system with no conflicting cohorts. The appropriate part of this course is:
The Lighthill report of 1973 is significant because it:

options.C: Preceded the withdrawal of British artificial intelligence funding

questions.question: Which of the following would make a capability claim engineering rather than marketing?

options.A: A statement that the system uses deep learning
options.B: A named benchmark, a stated baseline and a held-out result
options.C: An endorsement by a recognised expert
options.D: A live demonstration on chosen inputs

questions.question: Take one intelligent system you personally used in the last week. State its objective, the percepts available to it, and the actions it can take. Then state one situation in which it would act badly, and say whether the fault lies in the objective or in the percepts.
questions.modelAnswer: Answers vary. A complete response names one used system, its objective, available percepts, possible actions, one failure situation, and whether that failure follows from the stated objective or missing percepts.
rubric: Names a personally used intelligent system.
States its objective, percepts and actions.
Gives one situation where it acts badly.
Attributes the fault to the objective or percepts and explains why.
questions.source: Module 1, Check your understanding, Part B, question 1
questions.hint2: Use one recent system; classify its failure as an objective or percept problem.

questions.question: Both artificial intelligence winters followed the same three-step pattern. Describe the pattern in your own words in no more than eighty words, then apply it to one current claim about generative artificial intelligence.
questions.modelAnswer: A real technical result was generalised in public claims beyond its support, funded on those claims, and defunded when the gap became undeniable. Apply those three stages to one current generative-AI capability claim without extending the evidence beyond the handout's description.
rubric: States the real-result, inflated-claim and defunding pattern.
Uses no more than eighty words.
Applies the pattern to one generative-AI claim.
questions.source: Module 1, Check your understanding, Part B, question 2
questions.hint: Real result → broad claim → funding collapse.
questions.hint2: Apply the same three stages to a generative-AI capability claim.

questions.question: Explain, with an example from Philippine practice, a problem where the correct approach involves no machine learning at all. Justify why a learned model would be the wrong instrument.
questions.modelAnswer: Answers vary. A valid response uses a Philippine search, planning or constraint problem whose correctness is defined by rules that can be written down, and explains why pattern extraction from collected examples is unnecessary or unsuitable.
rubric: Uses an example from Philippine practice.
Explains that correctness is defined by explicit rules.
Justifies why learning from examples is the wrong instrument.
questions.source: Module 1, Check your understanding, Part B, question 3
questions.hint: Use a problem with explicit constraints.
questions.hint2: Search, planning or constraint satisfaction; correctness comes from written rules.

questions.question: Turing anticipated and answered nine objections in his 1950 paper. Choose the objection from consciousness or the mathematical objection, state it fairly, and evaluate whether the intervening seventy-six years have strengthened or weakened it.
questions.modelAnswer: Answers vary. State either the consciousness objection or mathematical objection fairly, then make and support a judgment about whether developments during the intervening seventy-six years strengthened or weakened it.
rubric: Chooses consciousness or the mathematical objection.
Evaluates whether seventy-six years strengthened or weakened it.
questions.source: Module 1, Check your understanding, Part B, question 4
questions.hint: Choose one objection; state it; judge it.
questions.hint2: Consciousness or mathematical objection + strengthened/weakened + reason.
